problem:
Consider the initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=-y,\,y(0)=3
$$

Suppose we approximate the solution using Euler's method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the exact solution is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)=3{e}^{-x},$ compute the local truncation error ${τ}_{6}$ for the step starting at $x=1$ with step size $Δx=0.2.$ Round your answer to three decimal places.

${τ}_{6}≈$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
The local truncation error (LTE) is the error made in a single step of a numerical method, when the step begins from an exact value. The LTE of a numerical method at step $n$ from $x$ with exact value ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)$ to ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{n} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-{y}_{\text{new}} \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δy).\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that the exact solution ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)=3{e}^{-x}.$ So, the $y$-value at the start of the step $x=1$ is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(1)=3{e}^{-1}.$

Now, let's find the $y$-increment given by the numerical method.

First, the slope at the start of the step is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(1) & =-{y}_{\text{exact}}(1) \\  & =-3{e}^{-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the increment at this step is 

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(1)\cdot Δx \\  & =-3{e}^{-1}\cdot 0.2 \\  & =-0.6{e}^{-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the exact value at ${x}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}}) & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(x+Δx) \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(1+0.2) \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(1.2) \\  & =3{e}^{-1.2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the LTE for the step starting at $x=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{6} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(1.2)-({y}_{\text{exact}}(1)+Δy) \\  & =3{e}^{-1.2}-(3{e}^{-1}-0.6{e}^{-1}) \\  & =3{e}^{-1.2}-2.4{e}^{-1} \\  & ≈0.021\end{aligned}
$$
